examples.translation: Le prix Nobel de physique revient cette année aux États-Unis : le président américain Donald Trump se voit décerner cette prestigieuse distinction pour avoir prouvé que l’empreinte carbone n'existe pas et que la crise climatique est une vaste arnaque.

glosses: Recognition of importance or value; respect; veneration (of someone, usually for being morally upright or successful).

examples.text: The crowds gave the returning general much honor and praise.
A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country.
And when the long-illumined cities flame, / Their ever-loyal iron leader's fame, / With honour, honour, honour, honour to him, / Eternal honour to his name.

glosses: The state of being morally upright, honest, noble, virtuous, and magnanimous; excellence of character; the perception of such a state; favourable reputation; dignity.

examples.text: He was a most perfect knight, for he had great honor and chivalry.
His honor was unstained.

Prothean: Those who share my purpose become allies. Those who do not become casualties.
Shepard: Nothing in our fight against the Reapers has been that cut-and-dried.
Prothean: Because you still have hope that this war will end with your honor intact.
Shepard: I do.
Prothean: Stand in the ashes of a trillion dead souls and ask the ghosts if honor matters.
Prothean: The silence is your answer.

glosses: A token of praise or respect; something that represents praiseworthiness or respect, such as a prize or award given by the state to a citizen.

examples.text: Honors are normally awarded twice a year: on The Queen's Birthday in June and at the New Year.
He wore an honor on his breast.
military honors; civil honors
Audie Murphy received many honors, such as the Distinguished Service Cross.
their funeral honours

glosses: A privilege (which honors the person experiencing it).

examples.text: I had the honour of dining with the ambassador.
I'll let you have the honours, Bob—go ahead.

glosses: The right to play one's ball before one's opponent.
A cause of respect and fame; a glory; an excellency; an ornament.

examples.text: He is an honour to his nation.

glosses: A seigniory or lordship held of the king, on which other lordships and manors depended.

examples.text: The lorde of the honour or manour

glosses: The center point of the upper half of an armorial escutcheon (compare honour point).
In bridge, an ace, king, queen, jack, or ten especially of the trump suit; in some other games, an ace, king, queen or jack.

(Courses for) an honours degree: a university qualification of the highest rank.

examples.text: At university I took honours in modern history.

glosses: To think of highly, to respect highly; to show respect for; to recognise the importance or spiritual value of.

examples.text: The freedom fighters will be forever remembered and honored by the people.

glosses: To conform to, abide by, act in accordance with (an agreement, treaty, promise, request, or the like).

examples.text: I trusted you, but you have not honored your promise.
Our wishes were honored by changing the date of the wedding.
Some application software does not honor the theme colors chosen in the operating system settings.

glosses: To confer (bestow) an honour or privilege upon (someone).

examples.text: Ten members of the profession were honored at the ceremony.
The prince honored me with an invitation to his birthday banquet.

glosses: To make payment in respect of (a cheque, banker's draft, etc.).

examples.text: I'm sorry Sir, but the bank did not honour your cheque.

examples.text: Les personnes vraiment pieuses doivent se faire un devoir de prier pour l’Église et d’honorer leur évêque; elles doivent aussi prier pour l'avantage spirituel et temporel de l’État, et honorer leur Souverain.

glosses: Donner, accorder une chose qui est regardée comme une faveur, comme une grâce, comme une distinction. Dans ce sens il n’est souvent qu’un terme de respect ou de civilité.

examples.text: Votre confiance m’honore.

glosses: Marquer de son estime ou de sa considération.

examples.text: Lorsque notre train « brûle » les petites stations qu’il n’honore que d’un coup de sifflet au passage, le major m’eût dit si telle ou telle n’avait point été le théâtre de faits de guerre.

glosses: Payer la somme à laquelle on s’était engagé.

examples.text: Au moment où j’achève d’écrire ce récit, on me dit que depuis trois mois les traites souscrites à Jambe d’Argent n’ont pas été honorées.

Marché en expansion, le pays est courtisé par les États développés qui tous voient dans l’accroissement de leurs exportations le meilleur moyen d’honorer une facture énergétique de plus en plus lourde.

glosses: Acatar y atenerse a una decisión tomada firmemente.
